extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners and third‑party requesters) handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance on conducting, processing, and deciding inter partes reexamination requests and prosecutions, including petition practice, examination scope, prior art handling, claim amendment limits, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU Director decision finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Each decision by the CRU Director concludes with a paragraph stating: 'This decision is final and nonappealable. See 35 U.S.C. 312(c) and 37 CFR 1.927. No further communication on this matter will be acknowledged or considered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU Director reviews petitions de novo and when issuing a decision that denies reconsideration the decision is final and nonappealable; parties should not expect further communications to be entertained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timing and extension requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester may seek review of a denial only by petitioning the Director under 37 CFR 1.927 and 1.181 within one (1) month of the mailing date of the decision denying the request for reexamination. An extension to file such a petition can be sought only by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with the appropriate fee to waive the time provisions of 37 CFR 1.927.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no petition is filed within one month CRU will process the reexamination as concluded. Petitions must comply strictly with the one‑month deadline unless a successful 1.183 petition (with fee) is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of granted petition decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition is granted, the decision of the CRU Director should include a sentence stating that an Office action will be mailed in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU Director signs the granting decision and forwards the file for mailing and PALM processing; supervisory staff may reassign the reexamination per 37 CFR 1.931(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment of reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner's determination failed to find any SNQ or RLP, reassignment to another examiner is the general rule. The reexamination proceeding is not normally reassigned to a primary or assistant examiner who was involved in any part of the original examination of the patent or its parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are only for unusual circumstances where no other examiner is available and capable; the CRU Director may permit reassignment to an original examiner in such limited situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All inter partes reexamination proceedings, including appeals to the Board, shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office, unless the Director determines there is good cause to suspend the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 314(c) mandates special dispatch; this affects handling of late submissions (e.g., after NIRC) and the overall statutory timeline for processing reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and written-communication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of the inter partes reexamination request, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third‑party requester shall be served on the other party. All communications between the Office and the parties directed to the merits must be in writing and filed with the Office for entry into the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will send the third‑party requester copies of communications sent to the patent owner. Each time the patent owner files a response, the third party has one opportunity to file written comments if received within 30 days after service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an inter partes reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(6), except for certain enumerated petitions (e.g., petitions to extend the period for response by a patent owner under § 1.956).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct fee is submitted with petitions; several narrow exceptions are specified in § 1.937(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on claim enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of the claims of the patent shall be permitted in an inter partes reexamination proceeding (35 U.S.C. 314(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim presented enlarges the scope where it is broader than each and every claim of the patent; a claim broadened in any one respect is considered broadening. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 314(a) should use form paragraph 26.03.01 and identify the broadened limitations (see MPEP § 1412.03 for guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination (patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an inter partes reexamination proceeding will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112. Issues other than these will not be resolved in an inter partes reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.906).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parties raise issues outside these bounds, the examiner should note their existence in the next Office action and may suggest filing a reissue application to resolve them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible bases for rejections (prior art and double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections in inter partes reexamination proceedings may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications under the relevant prior art regime, or double patenting (see MPEP §§ 2258 and 2258.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive treatment of art rejections follows the ex parte reexamination discussion analogously; admissions may also be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art sources to be considered by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary prior art comes from patents and printed publications cited in the request. Examiner must also consider patents/publications: (A) cited by another reexamination requester under 1.510/1.915; (B) cited by patent owner under duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.933/1.98); (C) discovered by the examiner; (D) of record in patent file from earlier examination; (E) of record from any 1.501 submission prior to the order if it complies with 1.98; (F) cited by the third‑party requester under appropriate circumstances pursuant to 1.948.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of consideration is normally limited by the degree to which the submitting party explained content and relevance. Examiner initials adjacent to citations do not imply further consideration beyond the stated extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference copy requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires a legible copy of: (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or the portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and US patent application publications unless required); (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing or the portion causing it to be listed; (4) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required copies can limit examiner consideration; for references not scanned into IFW, the patent record's commentary is the full extent of consideration unless parties supply copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting copending application copies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required nor permitted that parties submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (which can be mistaken for a new request/filing); rather, submitters may provide the application/proceeding serial/control number and its status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper submissions may be returned, expunged, or discarded at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The exception to the requirement for reference copies in 37 CFR 1.98(d)(1) does not apply to reexamination proceedings since a reexamination proceeding does not receive 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit from the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reexamination submissions with the stricter 1.98 copy requirements; cannot rely on 120 benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submissions after NIRC (post-NIRC requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) has been mailed, a submission of patents/printed publications or other information described in 37 CFR 1.98(a) filed thereafter requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee and must be accompanied by: (A) a factual accounting explaining why the information could not have been submitted earlier; (B) an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable; (C) an amendment to such claim(s) and an explanation how the amendment causes the claim(s) to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are necessary to interrupt the proceeding after NIRC in order to comply with the special dispatch mandate. The standards are at least as burdensome as withdrawing an application from issue under 37 CFR 1.313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing prior art on official forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided in 37 CFR 1.98. The examiner must list on form PTO‑892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent) all prior art patents or printed publications cited in the decision, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on these forms (and not lined through) will constitute the list of prior art considered in the reexamination; the reexamination certificate will note availability of the list via PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 (written description/enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new or amended claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims in the reexamination proceeding are to be examined for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP § 2258 discussion of 112 in ex parte reexamination applies analogously; the Office may perform a 35 U.S.C. 112 written description priority analysis during reexamination (see In re NTP, Inc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments must not enlarge claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification is amended in a reexamination proceeding, examiners should ensure that the amendment does not enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent. An amendment can enlarge claim scope by redefining claim term scope even if the claims themselves are unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully evaluate how specification changes affect claim term meanings and scope; treat such changes as potential broadening under 35 U.S.C. 314(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for rejecting broadened claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim which enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a). Form paragraph 26.03.01 is to be employed in making the rejection and the claim limitations considered to broaden the scope should be identified and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bracketed explanation identifying the limitations that broaden scope and reference MPEP § 2658 and § 1412.03 for guidance on what constitutes broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior adjudication (res judicata/collateral estoppel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held valid by a federal court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined during a reexamination proceeding. Res judicata based on a court holding in an infringement proceeding is not applicable in reexamination because the Office was not a party to the litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior decisions involve grounds not based on patents or printed publications, the examiner's Office action should clearly state that the claims have not been examined as to those grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester specificity requirement (37 CFR 1.915(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must 'set forth the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested' as required by 37 CFR 1.915(b). If a request fails to do so, that claim will generally not be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests lacking the required claim‑by‑claim articulation may result in claims being left unexamined; ensure the requester applies art to each claim requested for reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to reexamine non-requested claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to reexamine any claim for which reexamination has not been requested lies within the sole discretion of the Office and may be exercised based on the individual facts of the case. The Office may also initiate reexamination on its own initiative (35 U.S.C. 303(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art discovered during reexamination raises a substantial new question or reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail as to non‑requested claims, and raises a compelling rejection, such claims may be added during examination at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice not applicable in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction in a reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding claims directed to a 'separate and distinct' invention would be considered an enlargement of scope and is prohibited in reexamination (see Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP § 1412.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary amendments permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments necessary and incident to patentability may be considered in reexamination. For example, amendments to correct an inadvertent failure to claim foreign priority or to reflect continuing status relative to a parent application if necessary to overcome a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted ancillary amendments should be narrowly tailored to correct factual/legal defects relevant to patentability and not to broaden claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign and domestic priority guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on claiming foreign priority or domestic benefit in a reexamination proceeding is provided in MPEP § 2258.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP § 2258.02 for detail on when and how to claim priority/benefit during reexamination and related evidence/submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination under 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP § 1481. If a petition under 1.324 is granted, a separate Certificate of Correction will not be issued because the reexamination certificate will contain the change-of-inventorship information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File appropriate 1.324 petition with supporting evidence; the change will be merged into the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit use and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding. However, an affidavit under 1.131(a) may not be used to 'swear behind' a reference patent if the reference patent is claiming the same invention as the patent undergoing reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriate, use 1.131(c) affidavits or consider a reissue application for issues related to swearing behind references that are patents claiming the same invention (see MPEP § 718 and § 1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not considered in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions other than those based on patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C. 112 (for example, patentability based on public use or on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C.102(c), etc.) that are raised by a party will not be considered in the reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.906(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such issues are raised by the parties, the examiner may note their existence in the next Office action but should not independently raise them. Independently discovered non‑statutory issues also should not be noted in Office actions because 1.906(c) is directed only to issues 'raised by the patent owner or the third party requester.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination requests on reissued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reexamination filed on a patent after it has been reissued will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered; to reexamine a reissued patent a new request must be filed based on the reissue patent's specification and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment by the patent owner during reexamination should treat the changes made by the granted reissue patent as the text of the patent (including bracketing/underlining conventions). See MPEP § 2686.03 for timing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties and content of the first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up a patent in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner shall make a thorough study and investigation of the available prior art and make the examination complete as to applicable statutes/rules and patentability. The examiner must notify parties of the action and state reasons for any adverse action in an Office action, citing useful information or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rejecting claims for lack of novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references available, designate the particular part relied on when complex, clearly explain pertinence, and specify each rejected claim. Examiner may rely on admissions by the patent owner or requester and on facts within knowledge as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/(f)/(g) and 103(c) joint-research exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of assignment at the relevant time. To overcome a 103 rejection under 103(c)(2), the applicant must provide a statement concerning a joint research agreement and that the claimed invention resulted from activities within its scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'joint research agreement' exception requires (A) agreement in effect on or before the date invention was made, (B) invention made as a result of activities within the agreement's scope, and (C) the application discloses/ is amended to disclose the parties' names.
